items.title: Realign decision engine to README intent: percentile scoring, working priorities & dampening
items.body:
## Summary

Brings the Coaching Decision Engine in line with what the README promises — a single, governed flow (signals → gating → multi-axis scoring → **versioned prioritization** → deterministic selection → receipts, with recency dampening) — and fixes the core defects that were silently breaking it.

The headline before/after, verified end-to-end on the latest snapshot: recommendations went from effectively **1 topic** (99% "Reduce CRT"/"Reduce Talk Time", driven by tie-break order because every `priority_score` collapsed to 0) to a **balanced spread across 11 topics** driven by the data.

## What was broken

- **Two disagreeing scoring engines**; the pipeline used an inline placeholder `(level+trend+risk)*confidence` that ignored the configured weights.
- **Versioned weights wired to nonexistent keys** → `metric_weight` defaulted to 0.0 → every `priority_score` was 0 → ranking fell to tie-break order, not data.
- **Direction ignored** (`abs(gap)`), so strengths were coached as hard as deficits.
- **Dampening was dead code**; **governance flags unenforced**; **provenance** hand-edited; plus a `NameError` and a calc-name mismatch.
- **Scalar-magnitude scoring** let large-scale metrics (CRT ~1400) dominate rates near 0.1, compounded by **unit-mismatched benchmarks** (talk_time=50s, expert_5star=0.8 on a 1–5 scale, etc.).

## What this PR does

**Scoring — one direction-aware, percentile-based path** (`scoring/assemble.py`)
- `score_level` = agent percentile − benchmark percentile within the peer distribution, so metrics are comparable regardless of scale and a bad benchmark can't let one metric dominate. Only underperformance scores; `risk = level × (1 − confidence)`; `score_total` uses `priority_model`.
- Deletes the placeholder block in `run_pipeline.py` and the four thin `score_*.py` modules.

**Prioritization — versioned weights actually apply**
- `weights.py` resolves metric → category → `priorities.by_category`. `apply.py` uses the precomputed `score_total` (no double-weighting) and enforces `eligible_for_prioritization`.

**Recency dampening — wired end-to-end**
- New `coaching_history.sql.j2` extract + governed crosswalk (`coaching_history_map.yaml`, `behavior_selected → topic`), `ingestion/coaching_history.py` normalizer, rewritten `dampening.py` (correct week-diff window, multiply ×0.5). No-ops safely when no coaching history is present.

**Benchmarks**
- Fixed unit-mismatched defaults (erp→90, expert_5star→4.5, talk_time→900, crt→1200); stripped bogus copy-paste `by_call_type` placeholders; flagged `nsp100` for Ops.
- Added `_warn_benchmark_outliers` runtime guardrail that flags any benchmark sitting at a distribution extreme.

**Governance / housekeeping**
- Runtime-stamped `meta.data_snapshot`; fixed `build_signals` NameError + `average`→`avg`; removed stray files; updated README.

## Tests

Populated the five empty test stubs — **21 tests, all passing** — covering percentile/direction scoring, category-weight resolution, governance enforcement, dampening window math, coaching-history normalization, and calc-name handling.

## Notes / follow-ups (Ops-owned)

- `nsp100` and `one_call_resolution` benchmarks still need real target values (surfaced by the new runtime warning); percentile scoring contains the damage in the meantime.
- Completing the `behavior_selected → topic` crosswalk (unmapped values are logged each run).
- This PR also carries the pre-existing commit `11573ec` since `main` was behind the branch it was cut from.

items.title: Generic API rename, performance (cache + CSS-direct), README + benchmarks
items.body:
Everything since the rebrand (PR #9). Eight commits, grouped:

## Correctness / API
- **Generic API rename** — `generateScssDts → generateDts`, `scanModuleScss → scanModuleStylesheets`. They were never SCSS-specific (one pipeline handles `.scss`/`.css`/`.sass`, syntax detected per file). Nothing published under the new names yet, so no aliases.

## Performance
- **Persistent content cache** — an unchanged re-run skips the compile (size+mtime keyed on the `@use` closure, cross-process, `--no-cache` to opt out). Cold pays nothing (stat-only recording). Warm 1k SCSS: ~890ms → **~94ms**.
- **CSS-direct fast path** — plain `.module.css` skips Dart Sass entirely, straight to Lightning CSS. Byte-identical output (map only matters for non-literal classes, which CSS has none of). CSS cold 200: 423ms → **158ms**. Verified by exact nested-CSS map positions + real tsserver Go-to-Def on `.css`; back-to-back A/B confirmed **no SCSS regression** (+3%, noise).
- Native `sass-embedded`/`lightningcss` imported lazily, so a fully-cached run loads neither.

## Docs
- **Main README rewritten** — tighter, Vite-first, a "three ways to use it" list, prior-art merged into a numbers-forward Performance section, roadmap dropped. ~40% shorter. Deep material (how Go-to-Def works, full compatibility matrix) moved to `docs/details.md`.
- Package READMEs advertise zero-config / mix-any-style / fastest.

## Benchmarks
- Content cache + CSS-direct re-measured; added a 2000-file scenario; fixed the harness to skip regenerating huge fixtures on resume, and route fixtures through a `.noindex` dir so Spotlight stops spiking load.
- **Fresh full run on an idle machine** (worst σ/median 11.9%): styletyper leads every batch category — SCSS cold 3.4–9.1×, SCSS warm 3.4×, CSS cold/warm 2.2–5.9×.

## One honest note
Single-save **watch** latency (`bench/results/WATCH.md`): happy-css-modules 15ms leads styletyper 72ms (we debounce ~50ms to batch editor save-bursts). The README's Performance section claims cold/warm batch generation only, which we sweep — so nothing there is overstated.

Tests: 61 pass (7 new cache tests). build · lint · format · typecheck green.

# Task 105 — Function OS v0.2 Core Capability Benchmark, Adversarial Validation & Propagation

**Task:** `IGNITION-FUNCTION-OS-CORE-CAPABILITY-BENCHMARK-AND-ADVERSARIAL-VALIDATION-R1-20260730` (relay/tasks/105.md)
**Control commit:** `d2167c3472e32c0c053c7413c03219cac0389dcc` (origin/relay/current)
**Target:** `16f640045b3dc9d411f015a51e45de07299d31fc` (origin/main, PR #160 = task 104 terminal)
**Recovery path:** B/C — protocol-compliant re-execution from current `main` (no scope reduction)

## What was done

A preregistered, reproducible, adversarial benchmark of the **bounded** claims Function OS v0.2 actually makes. 479 deterministic cases across 3 strata (reference semantic / boundary adversarial / stateful lifecycle), 7 claims, independent oracle, frozen thresholds. Preregistration committed **before** any outcome-bearing run and enforced as an ancestor of every result commit (harness `ancestry_ok`).

### Verdicts (claim-level, bounded)

| Claim | Original target (FOS @ 16f64004, no repair) | After bounded N2 repair |
|---|---|---|
| SUPPORTED_SEMANTIC_FIDELITY (A1) | 0.9372 → PARTIALLY | 1.0000 → SUPPORTED |
| FAIL_CLOSED_LANGUAGE_BOUNDARY (A3) | SUPPORTED (false_accept=0) | SUPPORTED |
| CONTRACT_ENFORCEMENT (A2) | SUPPORTED | SUPPORTED |
| ARTIFACT_AND_TRACE_INTEGRITY (A4) | SUPPORTED (mutation_detection=1.0) | SUPPORTED |
| REGISTRY_REVISION_AND_ROLLBACK (A5) | SUPPORTED | SUPPORTED |
| BOUNDED_SEQUENTIAL_COMPOSITION (A6) | SUPPORTED | SUPPORTED |
| DETERMINISTIC_REPRODUCIBILITY | PENDING (replay_rate=1.0 on repaired code) | SUPPORTED |
| **Overall** | PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED_WITH_IDENTIFIED_FAILURES | SUPPORTED_WITHIN_BOUNDED_DOMAIN |

**Critical fail-open violations: 0** in both runs. The fail-closed boundary held (no forbidden construct silently executed; no failed execution entered the successful registry; all tamper/mutations detected).

### Defect found and bounded-repaired (reported separately, not masked)

Original-target run revealed a genuine implementation defect: `N2RepresentationEncoder._extract_expressions` used `expr.split('==')` (global split), breaking nested-equality postconditions such as `result == (x == y)` → unbalanced RHS → 25 `RUNTIME_ERROR` cases. Repaired to `split('==', 1)` (commit `1314ba80`) with a regression test; full suite 166 passed. The original failures are preserved in commit `aa803277` (RESULTS.json), not deleted or rewritten. The repair is an internal fix, not a change to the targeted reference commit or to any claimed capability.

### Closeout evidence (mapping to the 18 required items)

1. Formal task branch: `agent/function-os-core-capability-benchmark-r1-20260730` ✓
2. Ordinary PR targeting `main` (this PR) ✓
3. Immutable preregistration commit `5d664686` ancestor of all result commits ✓
4. Preserved original-target results (`aa803277`) ✓
5. Defect records + repaired-target results (`1314ba80`, `46471183`) ✓
6. Independent oracle + benchmark manifests with hashes (CORPUS_MANIFEST.json, RESULT_SCHEMA.json, oracle/reference.py) ✓
7. Claim-level + overall bounded verdicts (CLAIM_VERDICTS.json) ✓
8. Justified M/E/disposition + public-wording (function-os-candidate/v0.2/README.md §基准与已知缺陷) ✓
9. Genuine Zhiyuan-method editorial article (`docs/editorial/articles/007-*`, quality gate PASS) ✓
10. Article-impact propagation + review (MANIFEST/README updated; quality gate PASS) ✓
11. System-map impact declaration + regeneration + rendered review (NO_MAP_IMPACT; `system-map --check` → SYSTEM_MAP_DERIVED_OK nodes=49 edges=44) ✓
12–14. All required CI on exact final head + exact-head review (pending CI run on this PR) ✓
15. Ordinary merge of exact reviewed head (post-review) — pending
16. Post-merge `main` verification — pending
17. Fresh clean-clone rerun + deterministic verification — pending
18. Complete machine/human receipt on relay receipt branch + root — pending

## Scope discipline

This benchmark tests only the bounded claims v0.2 makes. It does **not** claim sandbox security, production readiness, or universal correctness. A favourable benchmark does not promote any unrelated Pointfire claim. Honest negative/null outcomes are valid completion.

## Merge request

Ordinary merge (no squash/rebase/force). After merge, a fresh clean-clone rerun + deterministic verification will be performed and the relay receipt written before declaring terminal state.

items.title: The documentation says exactly what the lifecycle guarantees (RV1909)
items.body:
The documentation says exactly what the lifecycle guarantees (RV1909, PR pending).

The README and the design principles carried "a full cost report" as a promise, and the twenty-first benchmark falsified it: the recovery run settled at $0.54 while its journal kept growing to $1.69. With the exit barrier (RV1903), the settle drain and the journal seal (RV1904) the promise became a lifecycle guarantee, and the docs now state the enforcement rather than the aspiration.

**The tightened claims.** The README and design principles name the mechanism: every child reaches a journaled terminal before `run_settle` exists, and the settled journal seals against late writes (`JournalSealedError` typed).

**The denominator map.** The observability guide states which number answers which question: the settled fold, the `run:end` totals, the terminal envelope and `invoiceFromJournal` are one fold that agrees by construction; a mid-run `budget:update` or a refusal's `spent` is an instant of the live ledger, correct for its moment and never the terminal; a later re-fold reproduces the settled figures byte for byte, because the seal forbids the journal to move. The benchmark's four views ($0.54 returned, $1.24 captured events, $1.46 refusal instant, $1.69 final journal) were honest clocks over a roster that kept moving; the lifecycle now stops the roster before the first terminal figure exists.

A documentation train: no code moves, and the mutation manifest stays at 342.

items.title: Present DeepSeek V4 Flash on one RTX PRO 6000
items.body:
## Why

The inherited landing page mixed this fork's single-card mapped-host work with
the broader GLM, Kimi, RTX 5090, multi-GPU, and NVMe-tier project history. That
made it difficult to see what this fork adds and which results were actually
validated on one RTX PRO 6000.

This PR is based on `rtx-pro6000` at `28254cd8`, which contains the generated
patch for runtime source `a2131dd7`. The earlier OCI v4 lineage remains
preserved as historical material and by the annotated
`history/oci-v4-20260802` tag.

## What changed

- Focuses the public landing page on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on one 96 GB RTX
  PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition.
- Documents five complete mapped target W2 layers 38-42, direct NUMA-local
  CUDA-mapped PCIe reads, and zero redundant complete GPU copies.
- Publishes the validated DSpark-4 shape with GPU-resident DSpark W2 layers
  43-45, 512 x 12 MiB FP4 correction, FP8 MLA KV, DeepGEMM, full and piecewise
  CUDA graphs, four sequences, and 2,048 maximum batched tokens.
- Adds the pinned native build, production launcher, and lightweight API
  validation path.
- Keeps Kacper's technical ownership prominent and links the broader upstream
  project for other models, GPUs, and execution configurations.
- Removes inherited benchmark tables from the top-level README while keeping
  their source data, reports, recipes, documentation, and history intact.
- Adds a tested renderer opt-out so report validation cannot reinsert those
  tables into the focused landing page.

The generated patch, `patch/FILES.txt`, and `patch/SOURCE.txt` are unchanged.

## Validated evidence

- Reasoning: **97.07/100**.
- Tool use: **30/30** exact selections and arguments.
- Combined suite-wall throughput: **53.44 tokens/s**.
- Model generation excluding harness overhead: approximately **56.49
  tokens/s**.
- Long context: **994,987 input tokens**, correct needle retrieval, 971.495 s
  prefill at 1,024.18 tokens/s, 975.550 s TTFT, 64.12 tokens/s decode, correct
  immediate follow-up, and 119 MiB minimum directly sampled physical VRAM

items.title: fix: 24 verified security and correctness defects + README rewrite
items.body:
## What this is

An end-to-end audit of the workspace, followed by fixes. Ten independent auditors covered one subsystem each (server core, auth, SQL/migrations, cache, agent-memory, CLI/client-core, JS packages, SDKs, build/CI/deploy, tests/docs). Every candidate defect was then handed to a separate reviewer whose job was to *refute* it.

**120 candidates → 107 confirmed → 13 refuted → 24 fixed here**, applied one at a time with a compile gate between each.

## Critical

| | |
|---|---|
| **WebSocket auth bypass** | `/ws` was mounted outside every auth layer and its local `validate_token` did no signature, expiry or session check — it accepted any non-empty string as any user, with full read and write access to the database. |
| **Fail-open record ownership** | `data_create` never wrote an `owner_id` triple, so the `if let Some(owner)` guard in get/patch/delete was skipped for every record the API itself created. Any authenticated user could read, patch or delete anyone's records. |
| **SQL injection** | The aggregation alias was interpolated into `jsonb_build_object` unescaped. |
| **Unauthenticated cache** | `/api/cache/*` was the one sub-router merged outside `require_auth_middleware` — unauthenticated read, write and enumeration of the shared cache. |

## Availability

The RESP3 decoder recursed once per nesting level, so roughly 40 KB of crafted input aborted the whole server process; array/map and bulk-string decoding also sized allocations directly from a client-supplied length header. Chunked upload assembled entire files into a single in-memory `Vec` — up to 256 GiB by the module's own limits. Prometheus labels were keyed on attacker-controlled path segments. The authenticated rate-limit key hashed only the JWT's constant prefix, so all users shared one bucket. The cache had no active expiry cycle and no memory bound, and bloom filters, HLLs and pub/sub channels survived both `DEL` and `FLUSHALL`.

## Correctness

Retraction mutated the original row without a new `tx_id`, so point-in-time reads and snapshot restore reconstructed the wrong state — restore silently deleted data. `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` were never pushed into SQL, so every list query materialized the entire entity type in memory. The row-level permission filter referenced a nonexistent attribute, making every non-admin list query return zero rows. The OAuth callback could not retrieve its PKCE verifier, so the browser flow always failed. The agent-memory embedding worker read and wrote columns present in no schema, and `schema.rs` defined `memory_entries`/`agent_sessions` incompatibly with the migration — whichever `CREATE` ran first won and broke the other consumer.

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` — clean apart from two pre-existing unused imports in `rest.rs:26,67`
- `cargo clippy --workspace` — 0 errors
- `cargo test --workspace` — **~1700 passing, 0 failing** (1438 in the `ddb-server` lib target). The `ddb-cache` L2 integration suite was run against a live Postgres, since it covers the largest single change in this diff.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm test` — all green

One regression was caught by the final gate and repaired: adding `WsState.permissions` updated three construction sites but missed the one in the CLI, which broke the entire `ddb-cli` crate.

## README

Rewritten against a fresh inventory of the real route table, crate layout and test counts. Four mermaid diagrams, each parsed against the mermaid version GitHub renders rather than eyeballed. It now separates implemented from planned and documents the known gaps honestly, drops the CI badge that showed green while `main` was failing, and repeats none of the benchmark multipliers that `CHANGELOG` 0.4.0 records as fabricated.

## Not fixed here — worth separate PRs

1. **No migration runner.** Only `001_initial.sql` is applied by `docker-compose.yml` and CI e2e; there is no `migrate!` anywhere in `packages/server/src`, so the 14 dated migrations are manual-only. The two new migrations here are defensively mirrored into the base files, so nothing breaks today.
2. **CI is red on `main`** — the workflow-wide `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings` plus the fmt step means `cargo test` never runs; the PHP and Python jobs mask failures with `|| echo`.
3. **SDK wire-contract drift** across all three SDKs: `accessToken` vs the server's `access_token`, `/api/query` expecting DarshanQL JSON rather than SQL, `operations` vs `ops`, and live-query clients listening for a `diff` message the server never sends.
4. **React/Angular/Next providers** import exports that do not exist (`createClient`/`DarshanClient`; the real export is `DarshJDB`), so every documented quick-start throws.
5. The release workflow builds only `-p ddb-server`, so the installer ships the server binary as `ddb` and the CLI is never built.

items.body:
## Phase 4 — Docker Containerization (P4-01 → P4-09)

This PR merges the complete Phase 4 Docker containerization implementation into `dev`. The branch adapts the multi-driver Spark + MPI architecture from local process simulation (Phase 3) into a real multi-container Docker cluster with NFS-backed shared storage and mpi4py coordination.

---

### What's Included

#### Infrastructure & Container Setup
- Docker multi-node cluster with isolated MPI network
- Container runtime dependency configuration
- Docker build context exclusions (`.dockerignore`)
- Generated artifact exclusions from Docker context

#### Workload Validation (P4-05 → P4-07)
- **P4-05**: Docker MPI WordCount validation — NFS shared storage, SSH connectivity, MPI hostfile, workload output artifacts
- **P4-06**: Docker MPI K-Means validation — WCSS parity-report checks against local baseline
- **P4-07**: Docker MPI Logistic Regression validation — accuracy parity-report checks against local baseline
- Synthetic dataset generation utilities for all workloads
- Docker entrypoint and worker processing support

#### MPI & Allreduce Fixes
- MPI worker entry point for WordCount dispatch
- Worker core dispatch path
- Worker MPI communicator forwarded to per-iteration Allreduce in K-Means
- Preserved legacy `multiprocessing` path with dummy communicator fallback
- Guard for zero-worker edge cases; corrected centroid comparison logic

#### Synchronization Overhead Benchmark (P4-08)
- `sync_overhead_benchmark.py` with `--baseline-workers` and `--baseline-cores` CLI args
- Fixed baseline module invocation: `run_baseline_kmeans` / `run_baseline_logreg` mapped to correct exported symbols in `mpj_spark.applications`

#### Deployment Launcher & CI (P4-09)
- `scripts/run_docker.sh`: idempotent Compose lifecycle launcher (`build`, `up`, `down`, `status`, `logs`, `shell`, `validate-p4-05/06/07`, `benchmark-p4-08`)
- `scripts/validate_p4_09.sh`: acceptance test (Bash syntax, Compose config render, CI workflow presence, README documentation check)
- `.github/workflows/p4-docker-validation.yml`: full smoke validation (Bash syntax → Compose config → image build → cluster startup → environment check → P4-09 acceptance → teardown)
- README updated: Docker Deployment Phase 4 section (prerequisites, quick start, workload validation commands, results location, cleanup)

#### Housekeeping
- Archived legacy local benchmark sweep (`chore(tests)`)
- IP config for local run

---

### Closes / Addresses

Closes #15
Closes #16
Closes #17
Closes #18
Closes #19
Closes #20
Closes #21
Closes #22
Closes #25
Closes #12

---

### Testing Checklist
- [ ] Docker cluster starts cleanly (`run_docker.sh up`)
- [ ] WordCount validation passes (`validate-p4-05`)
- [ ] K-Means WCSS parity within tolerance (`validate-p4-06`)
- [ ] LogReg accuracy parity within tolerance (`validate-p4-07`)
- [ ] Sync overhead benchmark runs end-to-end (`benchmark-p4-08`)
- [ ] P4-09 acceptance script passes (`validate_p4_09.sh`)
- [ ] CI workflow (`p4-docker-validation.yml`) passes on push

---

### Next Phase
Phase 5 (Multi-node Docker Swarm scale-out) and Phase 6 (ML-aware resource allocator integration) will be based off the `dev` branch after this merge.

items.title: Document matching engine design
items.body:
## What changed

- Adds a comprehensive design document covering goals, system boundaries, sequence ownership, book representation, invariants, command/event semantics, complexity bounds, concurrency, backpressure, protocol validation, persistence, recovery, failure behavior, verification, benchmarks, and production-hardening steps.
- Adds a reviewer-oriented navigation map, internal data-structure diagram, design-alternatives table, and claim-to-evidence matrix.
- Links the design document prominently from the README.
- Corrects the reference gateway's contiguous price ladder from an impractical one-billion-level range to the measured 9,000–11,000 range.

## Why

The implementation and verification were stronger than the architectural documentation. Reviewers could infer the design from code, but there was no single source explaining invariants, ownership contracts, worst-case work, durability boundaries, and the evidence supporting public claims.

Auditing the implementation while writing the document also exposed an impractical gateway startup configuration. The corrected range keeps the reference executable's preallocated ladder consistent with the benchmark configuration.

## Validation

- Clean CMake configure/build with warnings treated as errors.
- Focused and differential test executables pass locally.
- Linux `epoll` gateway cross-compiles with warnings treated as errors.
- Markdown links and whitespace checks pass.
- Repository attribution/privacy scan remains clean.

items.title: docs: retire competition framing and re-plan as open-source tracks
items.body:
## What

Two things merged into one consistent story:

1. **De-competition cleanup + roadmap rewrite** — the competition that framed this repo ended and v2.5.0 shipped, but the tracked docs still told a competition story.
2. **The previously unpushed `docs/three-document-split` branch** — the three-document split (CLAUDE.md = code map, ROADMAP.md = order of work, docs/project-status.md = evidence ledger, guarded by `tests/test_docs_coverage.py`) plus the newer platform truth from the AI for Thai participant guide.

### Changes

- **ROADMAP.md**: full rewrite. Retires Phase 0-4 (Phase 4 was a competition release gate) in favor of: where the project stands → outstanding Office acceptance → Track A detection accuracy (current focus; blind-set-before-tuning, gold-set adjudication, engine comparison, fine-tune/ONNX separated) → Track B hosted platform integration (guide-driven HTTP adapter scope, externally gated) → Track C open-source distribution and sustainability → trimmed Deferred list. A mapping note keeps historical ADR references to Phase 2/3 resolvable.
- **CLAUDE.md**: open-source project description with a one-line origin note; the three-document-split header; five storefronts including `desktop/` and `office-addin/` (previously absent from the map entirely); worker described as a provisional emulator; dead Horizon-plan references removed; the stale "first tagged run is still future" claim corrected.
- **docs/project-status.md**: three-doc header, updated vocabulary, new Detection benchmark row, Office row narrowed to Acceptance pending with the exact open scenarios, worker/platform rows rewritten to the participant guide's HTTP shape.
- **README.md**: storefront list and status reconciled with the above (Office remainder explicit, hosted adapter vs provisional worker, accuracy phase active against the gold benchmark).
- **AGENTS.md**: delivery order reflects reality (acceptance done except Office items, accuracy active, HTTP adapter per guide, worker = emulator).
- **docs/platform/ai-for-thai.md**, **docs/platform/ai-for-thai-spec-request.md**, **docs/acceptance/README.md**, **docs/architecture.md**: from the merged branch — guide's HTTP deployment shape, narrowed spec-request, Office local vs packaged evidence split.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**, **SECURITY.md**, **docs/release-process.md**, **docs/store/listing.md** (TH+EN), **docs/versioning-proposal.md** (now a dated advisory): competition wording removed or corrected.
- **ai_guard.py / app/server.py**: CLI and Swagger descriptions no longer say "PSU FTC 2026".
- **tests/test_docs_coverage.py** (new): every tracked top-level dir must appear in the code map, every storefront needs a status row, and the three documents must cross-reference.

Historical ADRs, CHANGELOG, and acceptance run records are deliberately untouched.

## Verification

- `pytest`: 855 passed, 16 skipped (includes the new docs-coverage guards)
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean
- `scripts/check_version.py`: OK (2.5.0)
- Residual sweep: remaining competition/PSU references are only in historical ADRs, CHANGELOG, .gitignore comments, the PSU LLM-gateway benchmark provider, and an injection-guard Thai fixture sentence.
